title: Smallness of modules with prescribed local models on a small ringed site
statement: Fix a Grothendieck universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a $\mathcal V$-small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with finite limits and terminal object $1$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings whose section sets belong to $\mathcal V$. Module sheaves have section sets in $\mathcal V$ and mean the sectionwise modules of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, fix a $\mathcal V$-small set $I_U$ and a family $(B_{U,t})_{t\in I_U}$ of module sheaves over $R|_U$ on the slice site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of $R$-module sheaves $M$ for which there is a covering family $\{U_j\to1\}_j$ and indices $t_j\in I_{U_j}$ with $M|_{U_j}\cong B_{U_j,t_j}$. Then $\mathcal P$ is $\mathcal V$-essentially small: there is a set $S\in\mathcal V$ and a family $(M_s)_{s\in S}$ of members of $\mathcal P$ such that every member of $\mathcal P$ is isomorphic to some $M_s$. No Noetherian, scheme, finite-generation or effectivity-of-arbitrary-descent-data hypothesis is imposed.
